%

\title{Exposure Concentration Under a Learned Ranker\\ Is a Cold-Start
       Effect:\\ A Convergence Test in a Simulated Matching Market}

\author{}
\date{}

\begin{document}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent
A recommender that decides which candidates a matching market's agents ever see
changes what a preference list means, because a preference over a truncated list
is not the preference that operates over the whole population. This paper
measures how far that goes and how long it lasts. A finite two-sided market of
1000 agents carries a four-dimensional trait vector and a private commitment
type; a neural collaborative filter produces top-20 shortlists; truncated
deferred acceptance clears the market over those alone. Exposure Gini under the
learned ranker exceeds an oracle's by $+0.0251$ $[+0.0155, +0.0347]$ over five
seeds at a hundred epochs. Extending to three hundred shows that is not a floor:
the gap peaks at $+0.3055$ and is below $0.001$ from about epoch 250, where it
stops being distinguishable from flat. That is a bounded residual, since a flat
tail is also what a very slow decay looks like. The ordering is positive in all
twelve cells of a parameter sweep, but its size varies fivefold, and the
attribution to the filter learning coverage fails in the one cell where coverage
never climbs, so the mechanism holds at one point, not generally. A companion
institutional comparison yields an interior welfare optimum. Five seeds carry
every headline and no parameter is calibrated.
\end{abstract}
